# Ordora — full summary

> Ordora is a digital-menu and online-ordering platform for restaurants, cafes, dessert shops, and cake shops. This file states only what the platform does, what it costs, and what it does not do. It contains no customer names, testimonials, ratings, or usage numbers, because none are published here.

## The product in one paragraph

A restaurant gets its own public menu page at a clean link of the form /restaurant?r=<slug>. Guests open it from a link or a QR code in a mobile browser — no app download and no guest account. The page shows the restaurant's logo, cover images in a carousel, an open/closed badge computed from its opening hours, today's hours, and its menu: categories, items with photos, prices, badges, and optional calories, prep time, allergen notes, and a previous price shown struck through with a saving. Guests add items to a cart, choose pickup or delivery, enter a name and WhatsApp number, and send the order. The order appears in the restaurant dashboard, where staff confirm, prepare, and complete it, and it can be shared through WhatsApp. A guest can also track an order by its code and reorder the same items from the confirmation screen or the tracking page.

## Pricing

- One monthly plan. The current price is shown on https://ordora.site/pricing; it was $4.99 per month when this file was written (October 2026).
- No commission is taken from a restaurant's orders.
- A free trial is offered; the pricing page and signup page state its current terms.

## What this plan does not include

- No card-payment gateway in this plan: payment is arranged with the restaurant as it is today.
- No standalone booking app and no standalone promotions app; table bookings are managed from the same restaurant dashboard.
- No multi-branch management and no multiple admin roles in this plan: one restaurant, one page, one monthly plan.
- More about the product: https://ordora.site/ordora-vs-menux

## Setup steps (HowTo)

1. Create a restaurant account and choose a slug (the public link).
2. Add categories and items with names, prices, and photos; set availability and opening hours.
3. Set branding: logo, cover images, colors, currency, delivery fee, and an optional promo banner.
4. Share the menu link or print the QR code for tables.
5. Receive orders in the dashboard and update their status; share summaries through WhatsApp.

## What Ordora does not do in this plan

- No card-payment gateway: ordering is a menu-and-order flow and payment is arranged with the restaurant.
- No booking app or promotions app as separate products (table bookings exist in the dashboard).
- No multi-branch management and no multiple admin roles.
- No transfer of orders to third-party delivery fleets.
